1a47e56deb170302.content: Manchester United have added Como starlet Nico Paz to their shortlist for 2027. According to Samuel Luckhurst , the Red Devils had already established their interest in Paz before he put in a five-star display against them in the Champions League last month. Nico Paz: The state of play (Photo by Marcos Brindicci/Getty Images) The attacker scored twice and assisted once as Como trounced United 4-1 in matchday three of the UCL, unsurprisingly earning himself the Man of the Match award at full-time. Now, there would be a ‘clear connection’ if Paz did make the move to Manchester, as compatriot Mauricio Pochettino will be in charge when club action resumes later this month. A graduate of Real Madrid’s academy, the European giants do have the option of activating a £67 million buy-back clause next summer. However, it would see Paz have to directly rival Jude Bellingham for a starting spot in the No.10 role, and he will want to be a nailed-on starter wherever he’s playing his football. United, meanwhile, could potentially offer him that. Could Paz be Bruno Fernandes’ long-term successor? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Bruno Fernandes, 32 , is out of contract at Old Trafford in June 2027. The board have the option of activating a 12-month extension, which they may opt to do in order to then sell him at the end of the season, with their long-serving talisman looking worlds apart from the best version of himself in a red shirt. He has also rejected two contract offers from United recently , seemingly suggesting he is ready to call it quits in M16 after what would be a six-and-a-half-year stay. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Fernandes’ goal and assist against Aston Villa on November 8 were his first goal contributions in the Premier League since United’s last win on August 30 against Ipswich Town, when he assisted and scored a hat-trick in the 5-2 victory. As for Paz’s return this campaign, the 22-year-old has notched a hugely impressive six goals and eight assists in just 14 matches across all competitions, including eight contributions in his four UCL appearances. f118af978c865f3c.title: Chelsea v Manchester City: Women’s Super League – live
f118af978c865f3c.text: The top two clubs in the WSL lock horns at Stamford Bridge in a seismic clash. Join Simon Burnton for live updates
f118af978c865f3c.content: Team news has landed, and here are the lineups: Chelsea Women: Hampton, Bronze, Buchanan, McCabe, Carpenter, Walsh, Potter, Thompson, Kaptein, Malard, Baltimore. Subs: Peng, Buurman, Nusken, Cuthbert, Bjorn, Las, Hamano, Brown, Beever-Jones. Man City Women: Yamashita, Beney, Rose, Knaak, Wamser, Coffey, Hasegawa, Fowler, Fujino, Hemp, Shaw. Subs: Cumings, Shimizu, Clinton, Mead, Miedema, Casparij, Blindkilde, Lohmann, Prior. Referee: Phoebe Cross. Hello world! So, it’s time. First against second, the club that won the league last season against the club that won the previous six in a row, and a game with the potential to define – and even decide – this season’s title race. Manchester City took over at the top of the table last week, when Lucy Bronze’s own-goal saw Chelsea drop two points – Everton managing to end a game in which they had 35% of possession, two touches in the opposition box (to Chelsea’s 55) and not even one single shot on target with a 1-1 draw – but there are only those two points between them, Chelsea have the better goal difference, and with the nearest challenger four points further back it seems likely, if not quite inevitable, that this season’s champions are playing in this game. There’s a long way to go, of course, but if City were to win, and stretch their lead to five points, it would take some overhauling. The really good news if this match does live up to expectations is that we won’t have to wait long for a second helping – there are only three rounds of WSL fixtures between this game and the return fixture at the Joie Stadium in January. Here’s the Press Association’s preview of this game, and the WSL weekend: Sonia Bompastor knows Chelsea will need to be “clinical” in their Women’s Super League clash with Manchester City. Saturday’s meeting between the top two takes place at Stamford Bridge and City enter the game as leaders having beaten West Ham 5-0 last weekend. Three points allowed City to move top after Chelsea were held to a 1-1 draw by Everton and the Blues endured further frustration this week with a goalless draw against Hacken in the Champions League. Chelsea dominated in Gothenburg but could not find the net and Bompastor admitted their last two games have been “frustrating”. She said: “It’s a good balance to have, to be able not to concede but also to be able to score. “I think the two last results have been frustrating for us so it’s good to see from the players’ reaction but also the staff reaction. “We have hunger going into the game tomorrow because I think at the end probably the Everton game was a game where we didn’t produce much on the pitch in terms of the attacking aspects. “Against Hacken, I think we were dominant in the game. So we need to keep working, I’m convinced tomorrow we’ll create opportunities and we will have to be clinical for sure. It’s an important game.” Only two points separate the teams and City boss Andree Jeglertz is looking forward to the occasion. He said: “I think these games are very special for everybody involved. We are really looking forward to an exciting day.” Jeglertz is hopeful that Niamh Charles, Beth Mead and Vivianne Miedema will be available. “All three of them actually were in the session (on Thursday) and I hope they will be available for Saturday,” Jeglertz added. “It looks good. We had a day off (on Wednesday) and (on Thursday) everybody is back, a good session, full of energy. I feel we are in a good place.” Saturday also sees Manchester United face Crystal Palace and Brighton host Liverpool, while fourth-placed Tottenham are aiming to build on back-to-back league wins when they come up against Everton. On Sunday, Aston Villa take on local rivals Birmingham and West Ham meet Charlton, who are yet to win a point this term. Third-placed London City Lionesses are also in action against Arsenal, with six points separating the two teams.

ca7dd4c2a3b07c0e.title: Mauricio Pochettino asked the US to believe in his project. Did he believe in it himself?
ca7dd4c2a3b07c0e.text: The coach’s tenure with the USMNT brought a whiplash of highs and lows. He met some goals but also left many with the impression he never truly bought in
ca7dd4c2a3b07c0e.content: It did not take US men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino very long to take his first big swing. He’d just taken the reins of the program after a disastrous performance at the 2024 Copa América cost his predecessor his job, with the first home World Cup in three decades looming on the horizon. The federation introduced him in New York City, on the 24th floor of a building overlooking the Hudson River. In short order, he was asked about the culture surrounding the program. In his answer, he invoked the four-time World Cup champion US women. “We need to believe that we can win,” Pochettino said that day in September 2024. “That we can win not only a game: We can win the World Cup.” It is the type of belief that feels almost alien to observers of the US men, the type of statement that American fans yearn to hear so badly from a coach yet also roll their eyes at. For years, fans of men’s soccer in the US have been desperate to taste glory, and for years they have developed an inferiority complex spurred along not only by results but by international perception. Even in the present day, with American players playing in Europe at the very highest level, the idea that the US could win a men’s World Cup feels borderline preposterous. That never stopped Pochettino from espousing his belief that the US should believe they could make a miraculous run in 2026 and win the whole thing. It was a mantra he returned to frequently during his time leading the team, publicly and privately, even in the weeks leading up to the tournament. Pochettino even told Donald Trump that the US could win it all, perhaps planting the seeds for an assist turned own-goal down the line. Belief is something that could attract even the most casual US fans, the type of newcomers whose previous experience with an American soccer coach came from Apple TV. Unfortunately for US fans, Pochettino’s actions never quite lined up with the inspirational speech. There was the near-constant stream of rumors attaching Pochettino to clubs in England, rumors he never really went out of his way to quash even before they tied him to the Manchester United job he has now accepted. In many ways this type of thing is unavoidable and understandable: bringing on a high-profile coach and expecting peace and quiet is the footballing equivalent of dating a supermodel and expecting no one else to make an advance. Yet too often it felt as if Pochettino was the one stoking the fire; it was not uncommon to wake up in the States and find social media feeds populated with clips of the Argentinian espousing the valor of the Premier League and even floating the idea of returning someday. This was never really shocking or unexpected and was far from offensive. Professional sports are fickle and players, coaches and administrators alike are wise to keep their options open and their bridges intact. Yet it was a bit galling to hear from someone brought in to galvanize the US’s players and fans ahead of a generational event: a home World Cup. Pochettino also seemed sometimes frustrated by the very thing he was in part brought in to help change: American soccer’s sometimes awkward place in America itself. After losing the 2025 Gold Cup final to Mexico in Houston, he went out of his way to criticize the idea that the US would play in front of a pro-Mexico crowd on home soil, an issue that predates Pochettino by decades and may well never be solved, one even the most cursory research would’ve revealed prior to arrival. He fairly criticized the lack of stakes in Major League Soccer and suggested that US players are coddled throughout their youth development while at the same time butting heads with media who dared question the effects of a group-stage loss to Turkey at this summer’s World Cup. In reality, he faced far less pressure as the head coach of the USMNT than he would have in most any other major footballing nation. All of it too often gave observers the feeling that Pochettino was never truly bought in. But then, there was the whiplash, which was palpable. As soon as one began to feel that way, there’d be a fresh injection of dopamine – the US’s 4-1 demolishing of Paraguay, for example, far and away their best-ever performance at a World Cup. And there was Poch, nearly in tears and belting out Country Roads, then speaking glowingly about America, American football and everything else that comes along with it. A few weeks later, they’d suffer a 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 that will go down as among the worst-ever performances by the US at a World Cup. Certainly the most traumatic. Athletes and coaches hate being asked about their legacies, in general. The question in and of itself sounds moribund, as if the person asked is about to ascend into the ether. Legacies, too, are tricky things – they often take years to materialize, and they’re sometimes just as quickly erased by shifting perceptions or the accomplishments of successors. Pochettino does not seem to be the kind of person who would mind being asked about his legacy; he actually seems more like one who would already have one in mind before departure. Yet when asked by the Guardian on Friday to define his lasting impact, he struggled to do so at first. “I am not arrogant,” Pochettino replied with a smile and a laugh. “Well, not arrogant enough. I am a little bit arrogant.” Eventually he relented. Pochettino’s lasting impact, the coach said, was largely down to relationships, to having done things the right way, in his mind. “The most valuable feeling that we get isn’t one victory, or that we helped in the program,” he said. “It is that relationship in the program – even when you cross the sea, you look and smile because I think you share the values that are very important in life, more important than anything else. That is our principal that we respect always.” Pochettino has always thought in big, broad, ambitious strokes and has executed those visions over the course of hi

9c7e79c35b7d364c.text: Darren Moore praises Shea Lacey's quality after the Manchester United winger scored twice for England Under-20s against Czech Republic. The post England U20 coach outlines what Shea Lacey must do to take his game to the next level appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
9c7e79c35b7d364c.content: Manchester United winger Shea Lacey has been one of The Red Devils’ shining lights in what has turned out to be one of their worst league starts. Ten league games into the 2026/27 season, it is disappointing that the Red Devils have only one win and just eight points, leaving them languishing in the relegation zone. These have been a frustrating few months, yet individual brilliance from certain players has still given fans hope that the team can turn things around. One player who has kept supporters looking forward to United games despite the side’s struggles is Lacey. His masterclass of a cameo against AS Roma electrified United’s right flank after a passive performance from Amad . He provided the assist for the winning goal, the clear highlight of his season so far. He had already delivered a quality display in United’s EFL Cup clash with Brighton & Hove Albion, only for Michael Carrick to overlook him in the matches that followed. Against Roma, however, he reminded everyone of his quality and then backed it up with another eye-catching cameo in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Praise from England Under-20 head coach Now, days after those impressive performances that should edge Lacey closer to a key role for the Red Devils, England Under-20 head coach Darren Moore has raved about the young attacker. Shea Lacey for England under 20 Stat Shea Lacey National team England U20 Caps 5 Goals 2 Years 2025– Source: Wikipedia · Updated 14 Nov 2026 “Not only is his game so exquisite in terms of on-the-ball, but there’s an end product in terms of his crosses, his deliveries, and his goal scoring,” Moore told reporters post-match, according to The Athletic . “What you want him to do is be consistent with it. Off the ball, I want him to do his work early and get him back into position early, and he’s getting better at that.” Lacey has a big future ahead Lacey is one of a kind, and Moore could not have put it better. The hope now is that he reaches his full potential. Moore was speaking after the United gem scored a brace in England Under-20s ’ 6-1 win over the Czech Republic Under-20s. A clash with Portugal Under-20s comes next for Lacey , giving him a chance to carry his momentum and push for a start at Anfield when United take on Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge . c9b13b2b3dd63901.text: Lisandro Martínez received mixed reviews from Argentine media after Argentina's 2-1 friendly defeat to Uruguay in Buenos Aires. The post Lisandro Martinez: Argentine media deliver verdict on Man United star after Uruguay defeat appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
c9b13b2b3dd63901.content: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez’s future remains up in the air after some poor performances this season. The Argentine picked up a red card against Chelsea at the end of last month and subsequently missed the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend. Martinez also stirred up controversy by directly questioning the club’s transfer activity after the defeat to Atletico Madrid last month. The 28 year old’s poor form this season has affected the Red Devils, who have conceded 30 goals in 15 games and are 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games. Despite his struggles, Martínez was picked by Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni for the November friendlies. The international break, as such, represented an opportunity for the player to clear his mind and regain his form. Martínez was in the starting XI as La Albiceleste stuttered to a 2-1 defeat. The United defender attempted 78 passes, completing 71 of them with 91% efficiency, and created one chance. He attempted four long balls, but none of them found their intended targets. Martínez won both of his ground duels, but failed to win either of his aerial duels. He also attempted one shot, which was off target. His performance has since been assessed by the Argentine media, who have all handed him similar ratings. Argentine press react to Martinez performance Martínez received a 5/10 rating from El Destape , who wrote: “He didn’t have any trouble in defence, was always well positioned and played his way out of defence with his usual flair, delivering low, precise passes into midfield. In the second half, a poor clearance by him into the centre of the box led to Balerdi’s own goal, making it 0–1.” BOLAVIP also gave the Argentine 5 out of 10, while noting: “His usual resilience and simplicity. Solid in one-on-one situations. He had no chance with Uruguay’s goals.” The United defender also received a 5/10 from La Página Millonaria , who held him partly responsible for one of Uruguay’s goals. The report states: “Just like Balerdi in the first half: a few well-timed interventions, some duels won, others lost, and little else. He was partly to blame for Uruguay’s first goal, with a clearance that rebounded off Balerdi.” Finally, Noticias Argentinas pointed out that Licha was caught out of position during the game and also gave him a rating of 5. The report added: “The header to clear the lobbed cross for the first goal fell short and struck Balerdi, resulting in an own goal. It was a well-organised performance from ‘Licha’, but he was caught out on a few occasions.” Martinez’s future remains unclear Martínez’s contract with United expires at the end of this season and he is yet to be handed a new deal. Recent reports suggest that Barcelona have stepped up their efforts to secure his signature. Meanwhile, Michael Carrick has vacated the hot seat at Old Trafford following the poor run and Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as his replacement. The Argentine defender will be hoping to impress his new manager and secure a place in his plans at the Theatre of Dreams. 46ab895ee0a982f3.title: Report: United Women 2 Crystal Palace 0
46ab895ee0a982f3.text: Eva Olid's Manchester United made it qw games unbeaten across all competitions with victory over Crystal Palace at the Progress with Unity Stadium, in Saturday's lunchtime clash.
46ab895ee0a982f3.content: Manchester United Women welcomed Crystal Palace to the Progress with Unity Stadium. First half Elisabeth Terland had the hosts’ first chance, but her effort from distance sailed over the bar. Phallon Tullis-Joyce had to pull off an impressive stop to keep her side level at the near post. Terland broke through and put the ball past the keeper, but it was ruled out for offside. The Norwegian was close again, but her effort trickled just wide of the post. Finally, Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier broke the deadlock. Manchester United midfielder Jess Park picked out Le Tissier, who smashed a strike into the bottom corner from 25 yards to perfectly mark her 150th match as a Red Devil. Jess Park, Julia Zigiotti and Simi Awujo all went close to scoring, but the Palace defence held firm and made an impressive stop on each occasion. Second half Palace started the second half with vigour, and Bethany England went close with a shot, but it trickled just wide of the goal. Le Tissier flicked the ball towards goal, but her effort went just wide. In the 65th minute, United made the game much more comfortable when they scored their second. Park played in Elisabeth Terland , and she kept her cool to slot the ball past the Palace keeper. The game became more transitional, and Lea Schüller almost added a third, but her shot went just over the crossbar. Teri doubles our lead! Watch the match live on @SkySportsWSL https://t.co/V4gluP4cv0 — Manchester United Women (@ManUtdWomen) November 14, 2026 The match petered out in a 2-0 win, and Eva Olid’s side made it 12 matches unbeaten in all competitions. United now find themselves fourth and just one point behind the Champions League places and London City Lionesses. 3c005a572d6e3335.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Incoming Man United manager makes bold Jason Wilcox demand
3c005a572d6e3335.text: Mauricio Pochettino reportedly wants Jason Wilcox replaced as Manchester United sporting director after taking charge at Old Trafford. The post Mauricio Pochettino: Incoming Man United manager makes bold Jason Wilcox demand appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
3c005a572d6e3335.content: Manchester United have tasked Mauricio Pochettino , the current USMNT manager, with salvaging their season after a dismal run left them 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games. The Red Devils have parted ways with Michael Carrick this week and appointed the Argentine as his replacement. Pochettino is reportedly set to leave his position next week to take charge at Old Trafford ahead of the crucial game against Liverpool. United will be hoping that Pochettino can get the team playing his high-intensity attacking football. However, for that to materialise, the Red Devils will also have to back the manager in the transfer market. The Argentine is expected to have sought assurances about squad reinforcements ahead of agreeing to take up the job. However, it now appears that the former Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) manager requested a specific change behind the scenes as well. Pochettino wants Jason Wilcox upgrade According to Football Insider , Pochettino wants United sporting director Jason Wilcox to be replaced. The report states: “Mauricio Pochettino wants Jason Wilcox replaced as Manchester United’s sporting director, sources have told Football Insider.” “Football Insider can reveal that Pochettino wants someone he can trust in charge of recruitment at Old Trafford. Discussions have already taken place between the Argentine and the United hierarchy over potential candidates for the key role.” “It is understood that a potential change in sporting director was key to the former Tottenham Hotspur manager coming to Old Trafford this season.” Manchester United 2026 summer signings under Jason Wilcox Window Player In/out From/to Fee Note Source 2026/27 Carlos Baleba Signed Brighton & Hove Albion £65.1m – SalarySport 2026/27 Andrey Santos Signed Chelsea £48.3m – SalarySport 2026/27 Youri Tielemans Signed Aston Villa £35.1m – SalarySport 2026/27 Karl Darlow Signed Leeds United – Free SalarySport 2026/27 Tynan Thompson Signed Tottenham Hotspur – Undisclosed Wikipedia 2026/27 Kit Margetson Signed Swansea City – Undisclosed Wikipedia 2026/27 Cristian Orozco Signed Fortaleza – Undisclosed Wikipedia 2026/27 Karim Cassim Signed Manchester City – Undisclosed Wikipedia 2026/27 David Eze Signed Manchester City – Undisclosed Wikipedia 2026/27 Isaac Konde Signed Liverpool – Undisclosed Wikipedia Fees: SalarySport and Wikipedia United’s winter plans may not please fans Wilcox has become unpopular among fans in recent times, especially after it was recently reported that he failed to sign any of Carrick’s four priority targets this summer. This included a disappointing attempt to win the race for Elliot Anderson , who ended up joining Manchester City. The report from Football Insider adds that Pochettino may not be handed all his transfer targets in the January transfer window. Instead, United are likely to use the opportunity to strengthen the defence, which has failed to impress this season and requires urgent attention. The report continues: “Football Insider understands that if there are to be additions, the club will focus on strengthening the defensive third, rather than anywhere else.” United signed Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba this summer to replace Casemiro , but none of them have managed to live up to the role. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person has explained how the Red Devils have struggled in the absence of the Brazilian, who is currently plying his trade with Inter Miami in the MLS. e88df37075f9cd5b.title: Ruthless Pochettino to ban one thing United players used to do after matches under Carrick - report
e88df37075f9cd5b.text: Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly set to intensify Manchester United's fitness work and end post-match days off for players. The post Ruthless Pochettino to ban one thing Man United players used to do after matches under Carrick appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
e88df37075f9cd5b.content: Mauricio Pochettino, the United States national team head coach, has reportedly been announced as Manchester United’s head coach and will take over the reins from November 18. After an incredible start to his reign, Michael Carrick lost his grip at the helm this term, with United languishing in the relegation zone after 10 games. The club legend ultimately paid the price with his job. Now, Pochettino would have to make drastic changes to pull the Red Devils out of their troubles. Mauricio Pochettino to ban players’ day off after games According to The Sun , Pochettino is set to “crack the whip” with his players to improve their much-criticised fitness. Carrick’s side received a lot of backlash for their lack of intensity this season, as the Englishman tried to implement a more possession-focused style with less emphasis on pressing. United reportedly currently sit 19th for total distance covered in the Premier League and 17th for high-speed running distance. Pochettino will be joined by his son, Sebastiano, who is also his fitness coach for the United States national team, to significantly improve the aforementioned metrics. Furthermore, it is understood that Pochettino is set to order United players to report at their Carrington training complex the day after games for recovery sessions. “Under Carrick, the squad were almost always off the day after a match,” the report states. Mauricio Pochettino – USMNT Stat From 10 September 2024 To present Matches 35 Wins 21 Draws 2 Losses 12 Win % 60.0% Source: Wikipedia · Updated 14 Nov 2026 How Mauricio Pochettino’s approach is different from his predecessors While Pochettino will arrive at Carrington with his own fitness coach, Carrick inherited Charlie Owen at United. Interestingly, Owen was not part of the coaching exodus this week. He has been the United fitness coach since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer promoted him in the summer of 2019. Ruben Amorim brought his own man, Paulo Barreira, who worked with him at Sporting CP and has now joined him at AC Milan. It is claimed that Amorim adjusted United’s training pattern so that their daily sessions became less intense as they approached matchday, ensuring the players were as fresh as possible. According to Samuel Luckhurst , players felt the Portuguese coach’s approach improved their durability. 38f9fc8313acd88b.title: Video: Le Tissier's stunning strike headlines Manchester United Women's win over Crystal Palace
38f9fc8313acd88b.text: Manchester United Women claimed a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace in the Women’s Super League on Saturday. The victory extends the Red Devils’ unbeaten run to 12 matches across all competitions. Man United exerted their dominance from the outset, pinning Palace back in their own half. Elisabeth Terland thought she had put United ahead early […] Article written by Henry Thornton .
38f9fc8313acd88b.content: Manchester United Women claimed a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace in the Women’s Super League on Saturday. The victory extends the Red Devils’ unbeaten run to 12 matches across all competitions. Man United exerted their dominance from the outset, pinning Palace back in their own half. Elisabeth Terland thought she had put United ahead early on with a lovely finish, but her effort was ruled out for offside. Terland came close to making United’s dominance count in the 16th minute when she drilled an effort towards the bottom corner, but her shot missed the target. Shortly afterward, Captain Maya Le Tissier broke the deadlock with a stunning strike. The defender received a pass from Jess Park before striking the ball into the bottom corner from range, marking her 150th appearance for United in style. An absolute ROCKET from Maya Le Tissier on her 150th United appearance! ? #BarclaysWSL | @ManUtdWomen pic.twitter.com/FcI0ol0KXf — Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 14, 2026 Terland looked to set up United’s second goal as she held the ball up before feeding Julia Zigiotti, who struck over the crossbar. The Mancunian giants continued to apply pressure, but could not double their lead before half-time. Palace created the first chance after the interval as Hayley Ladd won the ball high up the pitch and sent a pass through to Annabel Blanchard, but Le Tissier made a recovery run to avert the danger. The hosts threatened again when the ball dropped to Beth England, whose effort trickled just wide. Man United doubled their advantage in the 65th minute as Park threaded a pass to Terland. The Norwegian striker beat the goalkeeper before finding the net. The goal was Terland’s third of the season in the Women’s Super League and her first since scoring the equaliser against Manchester City. United managed the remainder of the game comfortably, securing their fifth victory in the Women’s Super League this season. Article written by Henry Thornton .

ed69bef0fd9519e0.title: Mauricio Pochettino to refuse Gary Neville instruction as Man United players learn fate
ed69bef0fd9519e0.text: Mauricio Pochettino will have some big decisions to make when he begins his role as Manchester United head coach
ed69bef0fd9519e0.body: Mauricio Pochettino akan memimpin Manchester United menjelang laga melawan Liverpool pada 22 November, sementara klub berada di posisi 18 Premier League. Mantan kapten Gary Neville menuntut Pochettino meminta dua bek pada Januari dan menekankan perlunya anggaran minimum, kata Neville di Stick to Football. Namun, menurut The Athletic, agen tak bernama memperkirakan Pochettino akan bekerja dengan skuad yang ada dan melakukan perubahan secara bertahap selama tiga hingga empat jendela transfer. United mengalami kekurangan bek kiri dan cedera Benjamin Sesko, serta hanya menghabiskan sembilan digit di dua jendela musim panas terakhir, dengan Patrick Dorgu satu‑satunya pemain dibayar lebih £20 juta dalam lima jendela musim dingin. Pada konferensi pers pertama, Pochettino mengaku keputusan sulit namun berterima kasih atas kesempatan memimpin United.
ed69bef0fd9519e0.label: PUNDIT
ed69bef0fd9519e0.body_en: Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United ahead of the league clash with Liverpool on November 22, with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League. Former captain Gary Neville urged him to demand two defenders in January and to secure a minimum transfer budget, Neville said on Stick to Football. The Athletic, citing an unnamed agent, predicts Pochettino will work with the current squad and make changes over three to four windows rather than a wholesale overhaul. United lack depth at left‑back and are missing Benjamin Sesko through injury; they have spent nine‑figure sums in the last two summer windows, with only Patrick Dorgu costing over £20 million in the past five winter windows. In his first press conference, Pochettino called the appointment a difficult decision and thanked fans for the opportunity.

5b2909f748e6bb8d.content: Manchester United are looking ahead to a pivotal January transfer window following a string of developments at Old Trafford. The Red Devils are 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games, with just one league win to their name this season. Michael Carrick’s failure to turn the season around despite investing over £150 million this summer has led to his losing his job earlier this week. The Englishman has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino , who is set to take charge at Old Trafford next week. There is an acceptance at the Theatre of Dreams that the current squad may require immediate improvements after failing to build on last season’s third-placed finish. Reports indicate that United, who have traditionally refrained from investing heavily in the winter, are going to go all out in the transfer market at the turn of the year to salvage their season. It now appears that they have already drawn up a plan for the winter transfer window. United planning to offload three players in January Speaking to talkSPORT , journalist Alex Crook suggested that Harry Maguire , Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martinez, who are all in the final 12 months of their contracts, could be on their way in January. He said: “There are big-name players coming to the end of their contracts at the end of this season.” “Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez – who could well be moved on in January. 716e3bf45c8efc37.content: Manchester United have reportedly made another mid-season managerial change following the club’s disastrous start to the campaign under Michael Carrick. Carrick was shown the exit door earlier this week after winning just one of the first 10 Premier League matches this term. However, the former head coach was far from United’s biggest problem, and it would take further changes to steady the ship in Manchester. Manchester United want to strengthen their defence in January New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino is inheriting a defence that has conceded the most goals across all competitions among the clubs in Europe’s top-five leagues. According to the Mirror , Manchester United are “ready to dip into the market” to strengthen their squad, with a “top defender” the number 1 priority. It is understood United have been reluctant to do business in the winter window, but there is an “acceptance that they need reinforcements in defence.” Jason Wilcox and his team frustratingly overlooked the area last summer, with an aim to address it in the summer of 2027. However, that decision has proven costly, resulting in the Red Devils regressing. Pochettino will now be backed in January with “major transfer funds” and will reportedly get a say on targets as part of United’s vision for success with their new manager. The Mirror adds that United are also likely to look at a forward, but a big-name striker is more likely for the summer. They reportedly intend to bring forward the plan for a defender to arrive in January. Three Premier League stars being eyed Recently, The Peoples Person relayed a report claiming United have three defenders on their radar ahead of the January transfer window. Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey have joined Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton on the list of potential targets. All three defenders are more physically dominant and better suited to playing in a high-line system than United’s current defenders, but it may prove very difficult to sign a top player from a Premier League club mid-season. Outside England, United have been strongly linked with Como defender Jacobo Ramón , who most recently showed his qualities in Como’s 4–1 win over United in the Champions League. fddf13ae1d685a99.text: Minute-by-minute updates: Join Scott Murray as Norway and Wales battle it out to try and avoid relegation from Nations League Group A4
fddf13ae1d685a99.content: 90 min +1: Haaland scaampers down the left. He’s clear. He should score, but in trying to sidefoot past Darlow at his near post, hits the outside of that upright and out for a goal kick. The flag goes up for offside, but it was super-tight and VAR might have overturned that decision … so that goes down as a big miss. 90 min: There will be six additional minutes. Remember what Manchester United did to Aston Villa with that exact amount of added time last weekend? Well, that. 89 min: Johnson responds by juggling the ball at speed down the left, and thrashing a shot into the side netting. Selvik might have got a micro-touch to that, but Wales aren’t getting the corner. Haaland, unflaapable, stutters his run-up and whips into the bottom right, having sent Darlow the wrong way. Game over. 87 min: Haaland waits patiently on the spot, ball in hand, as Wilson is booked for encroaching and then arguing about it. 86 min: The ball comes straight back at Wales down the middle. Davies carelessly cushions a header straight to Haaland, who rolls it forward for Schjelderup. Roberts challenges from behind, and clips him. An obvious spot kick, and a booking for Roberts as well. 85 min: Before the corner can be taken, Ryerson is replaced by Pedersen. Then Rodon heads Schjelderup’s delivery clear. However … 84 min: This is much better from Odegaard, who takes a touch in from the right to make room for a shot. He curls it towards the bottom left, and Darlow has to extend fully to fingertip around the post. That’s great play all round. 83 min: Odegaard strides down the right. He’s got three team-mates in the Wales box, but hoicks a dismal cross behind all of them. 81 min: It’s the Wales fans you can hear now, and Wilson and Brooks nearly open up Norway again with a crisp interchange down the inside-right channel. Nusa drops back to put a stop to it, but Wales are up for this. Norway can’t get out! Wilson dinks a pass down the inside-right channel for Brooks, who holds off Møller Wolfe, barges into the box, and dinks a delicate shot over Selvik and into the bottom right! Game on, and the Norway fans may have gone a little early with that Viking row. 78 min: Colwill latches onto a loose ball on the edge of the Norway D. He should do better than smack his shot straight at Selvik. But never mind, because … 77 min: Nothing comes of the corner, and so the crowd, giddy with relief, launch into their first Viking row of the night. 76 min: … and Wales nearly score it, Ampadu latching onto a Møller Wolfe half-clearance, aiming a stunning rising drive towards the top-left corner from the edge of the box. Selvik tips onto the top of his crossbar and out for a corner. Some shot, with a save to match it. 75 min: Some pinball in the Norway box. The ball drops to Roberts, who belts a cross from a very tight position on the left. Selvik handles well at his near post. Norway counter, Schjelderup’s shot from the edge of the D blocked. There’s another goal in this game, somewhere. 74 min: Berg crosses from the right. The ball’s only half cleared … so Wales are lucky that Moller Wolfe accidentally stands on it. That was a big opportunity to shoot under very little pressure. 72 min: … and that’s part of a triple change, with Brooks and Roberts also coming on. Cullen and James make way. 71 min: Colwill replaces the stricken Williams … 70 min: Williams pearls a speculative shot towards the bottom right. It’s no good, then he pulls up. It’s all suddenly unravelling for Wales. 69 min: Well, that was a significantly better first touch by Schjelderup than his hapless fellow sub Berg. This is a simple but beautiful goal. A ball’s shovelled down the left flank by Odegaard. Nusa reaches it and touches it infield. Haaland would be within his rights to shoot, but shuttles it further across for Schjelderup, who can’t miss from six yards. Into the bottom corner it goes. What a move. 67 min: Berg’s first touch is a slapstick masterpiece, as he kicks the ball up against his own startled face and out for a goal kick. 66 min: Norway make a double change. On come Schjelderup and Berg at the expense of Bobb and Aasgaard. When play restarts, Moller Wolfe crosses from the left for Haaland, but Dasilva does enough to put his man off. 65 min: Harris is immediately in the thick of it, spinning Heggem to the right of the Norway D and threading a shot towards the bottom right. Accurate, but not particularly powerful, and it’s easy for Selvik. 64 min: Wales replace the ineffective Koumas with Harris. 63 min: Nusa is a magnificent talent, though. But then we saw that at the World Cup, so it’s hardly breaking news. 61 min: The Ullevaal had fallen a little quiet before that goal. It’s not quiet now. Inspired, Aasgaard throws himself into a couple of 50-50s down the left, and nearly forces the ball forward for Nusa. Had he managed to complete his task, Nusa was away. The hosts have their tails up. The corner’s only half-cleared. The ball drops to Nusa on the edge of the box, to the left of the D. He takes a touch infield, sweeping James aside, before fizzling a low drive into the bottom left. Darlow has no chance. What a strike … and it would never have happened without that acrobatic trap a minute earlier. 58 min: Nusa takes down a difficult crossfield pass with an elegant leap and trap, then dribbles hard down the left, winning a corner off Williams, from which … 56 min: Rodon skittles Berge. Ryerson thinks a free kick is going to be awarded, so puts his hand on the ball then takes one. But the ref hasn’t whistled! Wales want a free kick of their own, but they don’t get that either. Norway are rewarded the restart. Some mild Welsh seething, but it’s all in the middle of the park so nothing much has been lost. A mildly amusing aside. 54 min: Bobb skates past Dasilva on the right. The Red Devils will reportedly be in the market for a defender and a striker. Transfer journalist Alex Crook claims the Mancunian giants could make a move for Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson in the winter transfer window. “Keep an […] Article written by Henry Thornton .
3cc3d3ac18802ebd.content: Manchester United are prepared to back new head coach Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window. The Red Devils will reportedly be in the market for a defender and a striker. Transfer journalist Alex Crook claims the Mancunian giants could make a move for Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson in the winter transfer window. “Keep an eye on Antonee Robinson for the left-back position,” he told talkSPORT . “He has been on Man United’s radar before and obviously plays under Pochettino for the USA.” Crook also said that the Mancunian giants could target Monaco striker Folarin Balogun. Man United should not target Robinson in January Robinson is one of the Premier League’s most impressive attacking full-backs. The 29-year-old combines explosive pace, overlapping runs and excellent crossing ability with impressive defensive qualities, making him reliable at both ends of the pitch. Robinson ranks in the 60th percentile for chances created and 85th for touches among full-backs in the Premier League this season. The 29-year-old ranks 90th for defensive contributions, underlining his offensive and defensive reliability. However, Man United need a younger left-back to replace Luke Shaw. Robinson’s injury history also raises concerns about his fitness, missing 26 games for both club and country since the 2024/25 season. The Red Devils should prioritise a move for Club Brugge’s Joaquin Seys over Robinson in the winter transfer window. Seys does not have Premier League experience like the Fulham star, but has the potential to become one of Europe’s finest left-backs. The 21-year-old’s aggression when pressing and defending makes him suited to Pochettino’s system. He also possesses impressive ball-carrying and crossing abilities. Seys could represent a better long-term option at left-back for Man United than Robinson. Stats from Transfermarkt & Fotmob Article written by Henry Thornton .

7e1d20265a98ae03.title: "More than a manager can ask": Eva Olid showers Man United Women star with praise
7e1d20265a98ae03.text: Eva Olid praises Maya Le Tissier and Jess Park after Manchester United Women's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace and discusses Celine Bizet. The post “More than a manager can ask”: Eva Olid showers Man United Women star with praise appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .
7e1d20265a98ae03.content: Manchester United Women defeated Crystal Palace 2-0 at the Progress with Unity Stadium. The result meant that United have now gone 12 matches unbeaten under Eva Olid. The Catalan coach spoke to the club’s media after the game. Maya Le Tissier strike England international Maya Le Tissier scored a long-distance strike to open the scoring on her 150th appearance for the club. Commenting on her impact, Olid said, “that [scoring on your debut and 150th appearance] is incredible, no? Because for a defender you expect the minimum, as you say, you need to defend well and help to build.” She continued, “but now she’s scoring goals and that is more than a manager can ask from a centre-back. She’s in a high level and yeah, I’m so happy for her.” Surprise tactics Explaining how Palace approached the game, she said, “you always want teams to come to press and then you can have more space. I think at the beginning they were doing well in the press in terms of wide areas and it was difficult, and we had some good moments of combinations, rotations, but it’s like that last moment in the box is difficult, but we managed to score two goals.” United conceded seven goals in their first two matches of the season but have been much tighter at the back recently. They have now kept four clean sheets in a row after the 2-0 victory today. Speaking about this, Olid asserted, “that [clean sheets] was the focus from the first two matches. We say we cannot just focus in attack and the fact that we concede goals in the first two games made us be so demanding that we need to keep the clean sheet.” She added, “at the same time we can enjoy attacking and trying to create chances, but it is so important that we keep that clean sheet.” Jess Park position Commenting on Jess Park, who added two assists today, Olid explained, “when I came to the club she was a right winger, and I think she’s a 10 [central attacking midfielder], but I wanted to wait the first weeks to see, but I think how I want to play, she’s better as a 10.” Finally, commenting on Celine Bizet’s return to WSL action, Olid stated, “we are working with her but she’s training well. It’s just now building that physicality because the rest [of her attributes], she’s totally fine. Wednesday, we have another game [v Everton] in the cup, she can keep building minutes, and then from there we’ll see where she is.” Date Competition H/A Opponent Score Result 14/11/2026 FA WSL H Crystal Palace W 2-0 W 08/11/2026 FA WSL A Aston Villa W 1-0 W 31/10/2026 FA WSL A Everton W 0-0 D 28/10/2026 WSL Cup H Burnley W 3-0 W 25/10/2026 FA WSL H Manchester City W 1-1 D 21/10/2026 WSL Cup A Liverpool W 5-3 W 18/10/2026 FA WSL A Charlton Athletic W 3-1 W 03/10/2026 FA WSL H Liverpool W 1-0 W 30/09/2026 WSL Cup A Durham W 5-1 W 27/09/2026 FA WSL H West Ham W 2-1 W 23/09/2026 WSL Cup H Sheffield United W 10-1 W 19/09/2026 FA WSL A Arsenal W 1-1 D 13/09/2026 FA WSL H Chelsea W 0-5 L 04/09/2026 FA WSL A London City Lionesses W 1-2 L Featured image by Jess Hornby via Getty Images online polls The post “More than a manager can ask”: Eva Olid showers Man United Women star with praise appeared first on Man United News And Transfer News | The Peoples Person .

Garcia handed Lammens his senior international debut against Spain in the FIFA World Cup quarter-finals. However, Lammens endured a difficult moment when a costly error allowed Spain to score a late winner. Despite that setback, Garcia has continued to […] Article written by Sanidhya Bhardwaj .
e4045bae5003709b.content: Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens has received a glowing endorsement from former Belgium manager Rudi Garcia. Garcia handed Lammens his senior international debut against Spain in the FIFA World Cup quarter-finals. However, Lammens endured a difficult moment when a costly error allowed Spain to score a late winner. Despite that setback, Garcia has continued to place enormous faith in the United shot-stopper. The 62-year-old told The Athletic : “I saw Senne in a restaurant and spoke about his adaptation because the Manchester United shirt is very heavy when you are a young player. Yet he wears it lightly. His big quality is that he’s not under pressure. “He’s a young goalkeeper and he needs to improve, but he has some big qualities. It can happen that he makes a big mistake against Spain, but my opinion is always the same about Senne. “Good guy, very good goalkeeper. He will be one of the best goalkeepers in the future. And playing for Manchester United is really proof of his huge qualities. He’s very calm, never panics. He reads situations well in the air and one-on-one. Good feet, too.” Senne Lammens must ignore the criticism The 24-year-old enjoyed a sensational debut season at Old Trafford last campaign, quickly establishing himself as a reliable presence between the posts. Remarkably, it was only his second senior season at club level, making his rapid development all the more impressive. Lammens has made significant strides over the past 12 months, and his progress deserves recognition rather than being overshadowed by a few recent mistakes. His arrival also provided a much-needed change after Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir struggled with costly errors throughout their time at United. The Belgian’s introduction was a breath of fresh air. Lammens is still developing and should not be expected to deliver flawless performances every week, particularly while United continue to struggle for defensive consistency. There is definitely room for improvement but not every goal conceded is his fault. His performances could improve further if new head coach Mauricio Pochettino succeeds in bringing greater structure and organisation to United’s defence.
